A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMWorld and contain readable main texts, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I. The retained content can be matched across reordering, relocation, and table renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 MLLMs, modality ablations, human evaluations, and error analyses, with numerical results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet evaluations in Tables 3 and 5.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction method is unchanged: manual video selection and annotation, automated video retrieval and summarization, and modality-specific QA generation remain the same. No new algorithmic component or model architecture is proposed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same human-annotated and two synthetic subsets, totaling 1,910 videos and 6,627 QA pairs across seven disciplines. Table 2, question categories, modality conditions, and appendix dataset statistics are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 5 add GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet to the existing model comparison. All previously evaluated models remain, and the comparator sets in the modality, reasoning, and human-comparison analyses are unchanged. This is a targeted extension of the existing comparison.

E3.justification: No changed data split, accuracy metric, judging procedure, or human-evaluation design is reported. Appendix C trims settings for models absent from the result tables and reiterates Gemini's ten-frame input already stated in v1. These edits do not establish a changed experimental protocol; Claude-specific settings are not supplied.

E4.justification: The modality ablations, difficulty analysis, evaluation-strategy comparison, judge validation, and qualitative error cases are retained. New Appendix B.4 and Table 8 tabulate the reasoning analysis already presented in Figure 4; they do not introduce a new analytical question or experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages with ± values in Table 3 and individual seed results in Table 5. The added models follow this existing reporting practice. No increased run count for retained models, new uncertainty procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 5 add cross-discipline and per-seed results for GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, with overall accuracies of 62.54 ± 0.79 and 54.54 ± 0.29. GPT-4o becomes the reported leader, above the retained GPT-4V result of 52.30 ± 0.49. Existing result rows remain unchanged; Table 8 supplies numerical detail for the existing Figure 4 analysis.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. No mathematical definition, assumption, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The benchmark's central contributions and world-model evaluation claims remain unchanged. The introduction changes the named best performer from GPT-4V to GPT-4o but retains 52.30%, contradicting v3 Table 3's 62.54%. The abstract and Section 4.3 still identify GPT-4V as best, leaving the revised headline claim inconsistently integrated.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 removes claims that judge validation quantifies GPT-4V's proficiency on human cognitive tasks and nuanced contextual understanding, and explicitly confines the discussion to performance as a judge. The main interpretations of model mechanisms, human/model differences, and hallucination and privacy limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C removes frame-count details for models lacking reported result rows, including ST-LLM and InternVL, simplifies Chat-UniVi naming, and restates Gemini's previously disclosed frame count. Appendix A changes the Croissant metadata link. The PDFs do not establish whether that revised link works; other code/data access and licensing information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds OpenAI (2024) and Anthropic (2024) references associated with the new evaluated models. Section 2, the benchmark comparison in Table 1, and the paper's broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix B reorders the seed, human-evaluation, and evaluation-strategy subsections and adds B.4. Other edits expand the appendix overview heading, shorten the judge-validation discussion, and refine terminology. The main narrative and section structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 5 gain model rows, and new Table 8 presents the existing reasoning plot numerically. Table 2 and Figure 6 move, while the judge-error and human-comparison tables are renumbered and relocated. Existing figures retain their visual content; the changes are localized table expansion and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The additional model evaluations and per-seed scores broaden the empirical evidence, and Table 8 makes Figure 4's results easier to inspect. However, v3 introduces central reporting inconsistencies: Table 3 gives GPT-4o 62.54%, the introduction assigns it 52.30%, and the abstract, table caption, and Section 4.3 retain outdated leadership claims. Claude's evaluation settings are also unspecified. These useful evidence additions and weakened reporting coherence prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
